prologo: There is a place where every faith meets and none of them blend. The ancients called it the Crossroads. Now they call it the arena.
Once a generation, a Codex wakes: a book with no author that holds the name of every god, and the door to everything that has no name.
Six champions have come to claim it. Five would guard it. One would open it.
And you? No one knows your name. No one saw you arrive. Only the sand of the arena kept your footprints.
Choose the faith you will carry. On the other side, the Abyss has already started counting: three, three, three.
epilogo_vitoria: The Triangle cracks. The Circle goes dark. Sigil 333 is nothing now but dry ink on a scrap of paper.
Silas Ashcombe sinks to his knees. For the first time in years, he calls into the dark, and the dark does not answer.
The Codex opens in your hands. Every god lives in its pages. The last one is blank, with room for your name.
You close the book. Some doors exist only so that someone will be wise enough to leave them shut.
The champions go home. The Abyss goes back to waiting. It always waits. Not today.
epilogo_derrota: Your journey ends here. The Codex closes, and the Crossroads forgets your footsteps.
Silas Ashcombe does not forget. Every challenger who falls is one less obstacle between him and the Abyss.
Get up. The tournament starts again, and somewhere below, something is still counting to three.

intro: You walked into the forest without asking permission. Curupira has already turned his feet around to lead you astray. I came to see if you can find your way back.
I'm not here for any book. I'm here because the man in black wants to tear a hole in the world, and every hole starts in a clearing.
Tupã is listening. If your faith is hollow, the thunder will know before I do.
Play. The forest will answer.
indigena.resposta_jogador: Then I'm asking now. Does it still count?
ao_vencer: Boitatá put out your fire before you even lit it. Come back when you've learned to listen.
No shame in losing to the forest. She's older than all of us.
ao_perder: You found the way. Few do. Curupira's going to sulk all week.
If the man in black opens the Abyss, there won't be a forest left for anyone. Don't let him. You hear me?
provocacoes: The forest takes back what's taken.
arcade_intro: I'm Moema Arani. The forest sent me to see who's making all this noise.
Play clean. Curupira plays dirty for me.
indigena.retrato_prompt: Half-body portrait of an Indigenous Brazilian woman in her early thirties, facing forward and looking directly at the viewer. She has warm brown skin, long straight black hair with a straight-cut fringe and calm dark eyes. Red urucum paint lines cross her cheekbones and black jenipapo geometric patterns cover her forearms. She wears a woven earth-brown cotton top that fully covers her chest, a headband of green and yellow parrot feathers and a green stone muiraquitã frog amulet on a cord. She holds a wooden maracá rattle decorated with feathers in her right hand. Dark Amazon rainforest at night behind her, giant tree roots and faint fireflies.

inicio: Ask permission before you sit in the clearing.
The forest is watching. Play fair.
carta_forte: Iara has sung. Now it's too late.
golpe: The forest charges for what's taken.
Hear that branch snap? That was you.
perdeu_carta: Back to the earth. The earth gives back.
Fine. The forest has deep roots.
vida_baixa: Curupira still has tracks to lead you astray.
Old trees bend. They don't fall easy.
vantagem: Lost? The way out is behind you.
The clearing's closing in. See it?
emote: Permission granted. For now.
Welcome to the forest. Watch your step.
You played with respect. I like that.
The forest saw. She remembers.
Think like the river: go around.
Listen to the wind first.
That's only the start of the trail.
The forest has more creatures than you think.

intro: Peace and all good, my son. Or my daughter. With that hood on, honestly, I can't tell.
I spent forty years pulling bad things out of good people. Now I've come to stop someone from pulling something far worse out of the Abyss.
Saint Michael holds the spear, Lazarus already got up once, and Jonah made it out of the fish. My deck has patience to spare.
Shall we? And if I lose, I promise not to bless you against your will.
cristianismo.resposta_jogador: Save the blessing for the end, Friar.
ao_vencer: That wasn't punishment, it was a lesson. The Ark doesn't open for people in a hurry.
Go in peace. But go train, too. The man in black won't show you my mercy.
ao_perder: David was small too. I should have remembered that before I underestimated you.
Take my blessing, like it or not. At the end of this tournament there's a door no card can close alone.
provocacoes: Even Jonah got out of the fish.
arcade_intro: Friar Bento Amaral, at your service. Exorcisms on Tuesdays, duels as needed.
I promise to play with charity. Charity doesn't mean easy.
cristianismo.retrato_prompt: Half-body portrait of an elderly Afro-Brazilian man of mixed African and Portuguese descent, about sixty-four years old, facing forward and looking directly at the viewer. He has warm tan-brown skin, a short white beard, a bald crown ringed by short white hair, deep laugh lines and kind but tired dark eyes. He wears a coarse brown Franciscan friar habit with the hood down, a knotted white rope belt and a purple stole draped over his shoulders. He holds a plain worn wooden cross in one hand and a small brass holy-water sprinkler in the other. Dark candlelit baroque chapel behind him, a gilded altar faintly glowing.

inicio: Peace and all good. And good luck, you'll need it.
I'll pray for you. After the match.
carta_forte: Saint Michael never misses with the spear.
Glory! That one came from above.
golpe: Even Jonah got out of the fish.
That hurt me more than you. Kidding.
perdeu_carta: The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away.
Rest now. I'll come back for you.
vida_baixa: I've still got faith. And three Hail Marys.
David won with a stone. I have cards.
vantagem: I'll bless you for free at the end.
emote: Peace and all good!
God bless you. Now play.
Well played, child. Don't let it go to your head.
Thank you. Humility thanks you too.
Thinking is a kind of prayer.
Easy. Golgotha wasn't built in a day.
A miracle? No. Practice.
Wait till you see the Last Judgment.

intro: No need to hurry. I waited a hundred and eighty years for this tournament. I can wait for you to shuffle.
The Jade Emperor does not care for doors left open to the void. And mind you, the void is something of a house specialty.
The Eight Immortals asked me to defeat you with balance. He Xiangu asked that I also do it politely.
Water does not beat stone by force. Let us find out whether you are stone or river.
taoismo.resposta_jogador: A hundred and eighty years? You look wonderful, ma'am.
ao_vencer: You pushed too hard and fell through to the other side. That, too, is the Tao.
Come back in a hundred years. I will still be here. Most likely with this same face.
ao_perder: Curious. I lost, and I feel lighter. Zhang Guolao would laugh at me, riding backwards on his donkey as always.
Take a peach. The man of the Abyss wants a world without end, and everything without end rots.
provocacoes: Nezha has come down from his cloud.
One Immortal falls. The other seven smile.
arcade_intro: Lin Yuehua, of Cloudy Peak. I came for tea, but I will accept a duel.
If I lose, blame the tea. If I win, thank the Tao.
taoismo.retrato_prompt: Half-body portrait of a young Han Chinese woman who looks about twenty-five years old, facing forward and looking directly at the viewer. She has pale ivory skin, calm dark almond-shaped eyes and long black hair gathered in a high topknot fixed with a green jade hairpin. She wears a high-collared deep blue Taoist priest robe closed up to the neck, embroidered with white clouds and cranes, with black trim and a round yin-yang medallion. She holds a white horsetail fly-whisk in one hand and a yellow paper fulu talisman with red brush script in the other. Misty dark mountain temple at night behind her, pine silhouettes and drifting incense smoke.

inicio: The tea cools. The match begins.
carta_forte: Nezha has come down from his cloud.
A leaf falls. The mountain smiles.
golpe: It was not strength. It was timing.
perdeu_carta: One Immortal falls. The other seven smile.
Back to the void. Good for her.
vida_baixa: A hundred and eighty years, and still I am surprised.
Bamboo bends. It does not break.
vantagem: You rush. The river is patient.
Do you feel the balance slipping away?
emote: Greetings, young one. Very young.
May the Tao walk with you.
Lovely. Almost balanced.
He Xiangu would applaud.
The void thinks, too.
Wait. The moment will come.
That? The Eight do that before breakfast.
You have not seen the Taiji yet.

intro: Finally! I thought the only fight here would be the line at the Crossroads. Grab your cards, the Ganges waits for no one.
Hanuman leapt an ocean out of loyalty. I only have to leap over you.
Vishnu comes down whenever dharma falters. A man trying to open the Abyss? That's a whole lot of faltering.
Krishna taught me to fight without clinging to the outcome. I'll be honest, though: I really like winning.
ao_vencer: Too fast? Kali doesn't apologize, and I learned from her.
Breathe, get up, come back. The wheel turns for everyone.
ao_perder: Ha! What a shot. Even Arjuna needed good advice before his battle.
Shiva dances one world to its end so another can be born. Go to the end of this tournament, and don't let this world end.
provocacoes: The wheel of Samsara brings everything back.
arcade_intro: Aditya Rao, of Varanasi. Bow ready, heart even readier.
No sermons, no waiting. Let's fight before the chai goes cold.
hinduismo.retrato_prompt: Half-body portrait of a young Indian man of about twenty-eight, facing forward and looking directly at the viewer. He has warm medium-brown skin, an athletic build, short wavy black hair, a neatly trimmed beard, bright confident dark eyes and a red and white tilak mark on his forehead. He wears a saffron cotton kurta closed at the collar, a deep red shawl draped over one shoulder, a rudraksha bead mala around his neck and a brass armband on his upper arm. He holds an ornate wooden longbow wrapped in gold thread. Dark riverside ghats of Varanasi at night behind him, small oil lamps floating on black water.

inicio: The Ganges doesn't wait. Neither do I.
carta_forte: That one's straight out of the Mahabharata.
perdeu_carta: The wheel of Samsara brings everything back.
vida_baixa: Krishna said fight without attachment. I'm trying!
I've still got arrows. I always have arrows.
vantagem: Breathe. The wheel turns for everyone.
One more arrow and it's over.
emote: Namaste! Now aim.
Hey there! Ready to run?
Ha! Well played, really!
Respect. But I'm still winning.
Think fast, the Ganges is flowing.
Hmm is good. Too much hmm is a nap.
Right? I liked it too!
Wait till Shiva dances.

intro: Sit down, child. No, it's not tea. Or it is. Depends how much you annoy me.
Baba Yaga taught me that every visitor is either a guest or dinner. I haven't decided about you yet.
Hecate guards the crossroads, and this tournament is the biggest one I've ever seen. Somebody has to sweep the doorstep before the magus opens that door.
The man of the Triangle thinks the Abyss is a tool. I think it's a mouth. And mouths eat.
ao_vencer: Don't cry. A black cat has nine lives; you've got at least two.
Come back when the evil eye wears off. And keep salt in your pocket.
ao_perder: Well, well. The Morrígan warned me through her crows, and I, stubborn old woman, wouldn't read the signs.
Take a witch bottle. Bury it by the magus's door. Or throw it at his head, that works too.
provocacoes: Hecate holds the torch. I hold the broom.
My cat still has eight lives, see?
arcade_intro: Ilka Wrona. Witch, grandmother and terrible loser.
Shuffle already. The cauldron won't stir itself.
bruxaria.retrato_prompt: Half-body portrait of an elderly Polish woman of about seventy, facing forward and looking directly at the viewer. She has pale weathered skin with deep wrinkles, sharp grey-green eyes, a strong nose, thin lips set in a wry smile and a long silver braid falling over one shoulder. She wears a high-necked black wool dress that fully covers her chest, a fringed black shawl embroidered with red roses and a necklace of dried rowan berries. A black crow perches on her shoulder. She holds a small glass witch bottle filled with iron pins, herbs and red thread. Dark misty birch-forest crossroads at night behind her, a single lantern glowing.

inicio: Sit. And don't touch the cauldron.
carta_forte: Hecate holds the torch. I hold the broom.
Look at my cat. Isn't he handsome?
This one came straight out of the cauldron.
golpe: Did it hurt? Rub some salt on it.
The crows told me where to hit.
perdeu_carta: My cat still has eight lives, you know.
Noted. In my book of shadows.
vida_baixa: The Morrígan is laughing at me. Let her.
emote: Hello, child. Wipe your feet.
Greetings. The cat says hello too.
Well played? I know. Thank you.
Hmph. Beginner's luck.
Think, think. I'll wait. I'm knitting.
Hmm is the sound the cauldron makes.
Wow is nothing. Wait for Baba Yaga.
Liked that? There's more in the pantry.

intro: So you are the last. Fascinating. Five champions brought down, just so I could have the pleasure of bringing down the sixth.
The Triangle of Art is drawn. The Circle is closed. Only Sigil 333 remains, and the Codex is the ink. Thank you for bringing me my ink.
Dee and Kelley spoke with angels and fled in terror. I looked into the Abyss, and the Abyss asked me the way home.
Choronzon is not a demon. It is the end of the self. Everything that dissolves in it becomes three hundred and thirty-three shards of silence.
alta_magia.resposta_jogador: Your Abyss will have to wait.
ao_vencer: Three, three, three. Do you hear it? That is your name being forgotten, syllable by syllable, at the edge of the Abyss.
Thank you for the Codex. Do not worry: on the other side, no one will miss you. Not even you.
ao_perder: Impossible. The Circle was sealed. I traced every line in the sand myself... Who erased the line? WHO ERASED THE LINE?
You did not win. You only delayed it. The Abyss is never in a hurry, and Choronzon has every shape in the world to come back in.
provocacoes: Dantalion, bring me what is theirs.
Three, three, three. Your Cornucopia cracks.
One piece fewer. The Abyss didn't notice.
arcade_intro: Silas Ashcombe. I trace circles, open triangles and close fates. Stay inside the circle, please. For your own safety.
Do not leave the circle, whatever happens. The last one who did is still being gathered up, piece by piece, in the Abyss.
alta_magia.retrato_prompt: Half-body portrait of a gaunt white Englishman in his mid-fifties, facing forward and looking directly at the viewer. He has pale sallow skin, hollow cheeks, piercing ice-blue eyes, long silver hair tied back at the nape and a neatly trimmed silver goatee. He wears a high-collared black ceremonial robe with crimson lining, closed to the throat, and a plain golden triangle pendant, a simple upward-pointing triangle with a single dot in its center, hanging on a chain over his chest. He holds a black wand tipped with a silver triangle in one hand and a red wax sigil disc engraved with the number 333 in the other. Dark desert night behind him, a triangle traced in the sand glowing faintly.

inicio: The Circle is closed. You are inside it.
Let us begin. The Abyss grows impatient for me.
carta_forte: Dantalion, bring me what is theirs.
Observe the Art. Do not try to understand it.
golpe: Three, three, three. Your Cornucopia cracks.
Every wound is a letter of my sigil.
perdeu_carta: One piece fewer. The Abyss didn't even notice.
It was already three hundred and thirty-three pieces.
vantagem: Your name is already being forgotten.
emote: Greetings. They will be your last.
Welcome to the Circle.
I know. I always know.
Compliment recorded in the Codex.
Think. The Abyss is thinking of you, too.
Hesitation. Delicious.
That was only the first seal.
Wait for Sigil 333.
